newsitem.title: USA: Union Camp says earnings decline from prices.
newsitem.headline: Union Camp says earnings decline from prices.

text.p: Union Camp Corp said Monday that its third quarter decline was from the lower product prices, but that prices were improving.

The company said the uncoated paper markets experienced improved activity as the quarter progressed. Prices, although modestly below the prior quarter average, also improved. Further price restoration is expected in the fourth quarter.

Earlier, the company reported third quarter net income of $14 million, or $0.21 per share, down from second quarter 1996 earnings of $18 million, or $0.26 per share, and below third quarter 1995 earnings of $130 million, or $1.85 per share.

Sales for the period were $1.0 billion, compared to $934 million in the second quarter of 1996 and $1.1 billion in the third quarter of 1995. Included in third quarter 1996 sales is $112 million from Alling & Cory, which the company acquired in August.

In the packaging markets, demand for corrugated containers strengthened during the quarter and prices began to stabilize near the end of the period. Demand for linerboard increased significantly in both the domestic and export markets.These improved market conditions have led to price increase announcements for both linerboard and corrugated containers.

Within Union Camp's UCC.N non-paper operations, building products income was well above both the previous quarter of this year and the third quarter of last year, principally a result of higher lumber prices. Chemical segment operating income was slightly below this year's second quarter and down from last year's third quarter.

"Recent market activity in our major paper product lines is encouraging," said W. Craig McClelland, chairman of the board and chief executive officer. "Our facilities are also operating well. As we move through the fourth quarter into 1997, we expect to see more favorable operating rates and improved pricing. We believe our businesses are well positioned to capitalize on improving market conditions."
